questions.question:
With reference to the history of India, consider the following Delhi Sultanate dynasties:

1. Tughlaq

2. Khilji

3. Sayyid

4. Lodi

Arrange the above in chronological order starting from the earliest?
questions.solution:
**Khilji Dynasty(1290-1320 AD):.......................(2)**

 
• It was** marked as the zenith of Muslim imperialism.**
 
• **Jalaluddin Khilji was the founder.**

**Tughlaq Dynasty(1320-1414 AD):..................(1)**

 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the founder of the dynasty.**
 
• He founded Tughlaqabad city near Delhi.

**Sayyid Dynasty(1414-1451 AD):.....................(3)**

 
• Founded by **Khizr Khan.**
 
• He was the governor of Multan and Timur's deputy in India. He marched on behalf of Timur and took possession of Delhi in 1414 AD.

**Lodi Dynasty(1451- 1526 AD):........................(4)**

 
• They succeeded Syyadis(1414-1451 AD) Dynasty.
 
• **Bahalol Lodi was the founder.**
 
• **Accordingly, the 2-1-3-4 sequence is correct. Hence, option B is correct.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the last ruler of the Mughal Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah II**, also known as **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, was the last ruler of the Mughal Empire.
 
• He ascended the throne in **1837** and ruled until **1857**, when the British ended the Mughal rule after the revolt of 1857.
 
• Bahadur Shah II was more of a symbolic leader during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, as actual military control was held by Indian leaders like Rani Lakshmibai and Nana Sahib.
 
• After the defeat of the rebellion, he was captured by the British, tried, and exiled to **Rangoon (modern-day Yangon, Myanmar)**, where he died in **1862**.
 
• His reign marked the end of the Mughal Empire and the beginning of British dominance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Empire:**

 
 
• The Mughal Empire was established by **Babur** in **1526** after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the Battle of Panipat.
 
• It was one of the largest empires in India and contributed significantly to Indian culture, architecture, and administration.
 
 
 
• **1857 Rebellion:**
 
 
• Also known as the **First War of Indian Independence**, it was a widespread uprising against British rule.
 
• Bahadur Shah II was declared the symbolic leader of the rebellion by Indian forces.
 
 
 
• **Exile of Bahadur Shah II:**
 
 
• After his capture, the British exiled him to Rangoon, where he lived his remaining years in poverty and isolation.
 
• His death in 1862 marked the end of the Mughal dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar is remembered for his poetry, especially his poignant verses reflecting his exile and loss.
 
• He symbolizes the last flicker of Mughal sovereignty before the British established complete control over India.

questions.question: ‘Ashtadhyayi’, written by Sanskrit scholar Panini, is a book on ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**grammar**__.

__
 
• Ashtadhyayi was written by Indian grammarian Panini during the 6th to 5th century BCE__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Ashtadhyayi sets the work standard for the Sanskrit language. 
 
• It sums up in 4,000 sutras that had evolved in the Vedic religion.
 
• Panini divided his work into eight chapters, each of which is further divided into quarter chapters.
 
• Beyond defining the morphology and syntax of Sanskrit language, Ashtadhyayi distinguishes between usage in the spoken language and usage that is proper to the language of the sacred texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Vedavyasa: He is the author of Mahabharata.
 
• Shukadeva: He is the main narrator of Bhagavata Purana.
 
• Valmiki: He is the author of the epic Ramayana.

questions.question: Which ruler of the Slave Dynasty shifted his capital from Lahore to Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iltutmish.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mamluk Dynasty is also called the Slave Dynasty.
 
• **Iltutmish** ruled the Ghurid regions of northern India.
 
• He was a Turkish slave born in Central Asia.
 
• Iltutmish was the** greatest of the slave rulers of Delhi**, who shifted his capital from Lahore to Delhi. 
 
• He **completed the construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the Qutb Minar.**
 
• He introduced the two coins of the Sultanate, the silver tanka, and the copper jital.
 
• He also **introduced the Iqtadari system** in which the kingdom was divided into Iqtas which were assigned to nobles in exchange for a salary.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Iltutmish’s forces captured Bihar in the 1210s and invaded Bengal in 1225.
 
• He **died in 1236 **and was succeeded by his daughter Razia Sultana as he did not consider his sons equal to the task.

**Tomb of Iltutmish: Delhi (Close to Qutub Minar)**

 
• The tomb of Shamsuddin Iltutmish is historically an important monument of Delhi under the management of the ASI.
 
• Located to the northwest of the Quwwatu'l Islam mosque in Delhi, **it was built in 1235 by Iltutmish himself.**

__
 
• **The Indian Struggle, 1920–1942 is a two-part book by the Indian nationalist leader Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose that covers the 1920–1942 history of the Indian independence movement to end British imperial rule over India**__. 

 __
 
• In 1927 Katherine Mayo, a foreign journalist, visited India.
 
• She wrote a book called 'Mother India'.
 
• It was about Indian civilization, culture, and life. She saw only sheer ignorance and filth in India and nothing good or decent.
 
• People who were opposed to the freedom of India had given money for the publication of Miss Mayo's book.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He joined the Indian National Congress during the Indian Independence Movement and became a major leader from the region of Bihar and Maharashtra. 
 
 
 
• **India Wins Freedom is an enlightening account of the partition from the author, Maulana Azad’s perspective**.
 
 
• It includes his personal experiences when India became independent and his ideas on freedom and liberty.
 
• The book takes the form of an autobiographical narrative and goes over the happenings of the Indian Independence movement.
 
 
 
• In response to that book,** Lala Lajpat Rai wrote the book unhappy India book**.
 
 
• In this book, Lala Lajpat Rai gave a fitting reply to the false propaganda of Miss Mayo.
 
• In this book, Lala Lajpat Rai compared Indian society with the contemporary USA and Britain.

questions.question: In which year Shivaji was crowned as Chhatrapati (sovereign) of the new Maratha Kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1674 AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shivaji Maharaj was crowned as Chhatrapati (sovereign) of the Maratha Kingdom on **6th June 1674 AD** at Raigad Fort.
 
• This event marked the formal establishment of the Maratha Empire, with Shivaji taking the title of "Chhatrapati" to signify his sovereignty.
 
• The coronation ceremony was conducted by **Gaga Bhatt**, a renowned scholar from Varanasi, who declared Shivaji as a legitimate ruler according to ancient Hindu traditions.
 
• Shivaji adopted the title of "**Kshatriya Kulavantas**" to emphasize his lineage and position as a warrior king.
 
• During the coronation, Shivaji introduced administrative reforms, including the establishment of **Ashta Pradhan Mandal**, an eight-member council of ministers to govern the kingdom efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1699 AD**

 
 
• This year is significant in Indian history due to the establishment of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh, the 10th Sikh Guru.
 
• The Khalsa was created on **13th April 1699**, during the festival of Vaisakhi, to organize Sikhs into a martial community dedicated to protecting their faith and upholding justice.
 
• This event marked a milestone in Sikhism but is unrelated to Shivaji’s coronation or the Maratha Empire.
 
 
 
• **1687 AD**
 
 
• In 1687, the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb captured the Golconda Fort, defeating the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
 
• This event was part of Aurangzeb’s Deccan campaigns, aiming to consolidate Mughal rule in southern India.
 
• It does not pertain to Shivaji’s coronation or the Maratha Empire.
 
 
 
• **1688 AD**
 
 
• 1688 marks the beginning of the Mughal-Maratha conflicts after Shivaji’s death.
 
• During this period, Aurangzeb intensified his campaigns against the Marathas, leading to prolonged warfare in the Deccan region.

questions.question: With whom did chatrapati shivaji maharaj sign the Treaty of Purandar?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Treaty of Purandar** was signed in **1665**.
 
• The treaty was signed between **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj** and **Raja Jai Singh I**, a general of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• According to the terms, Shivaji had to surrender **23 forts** to the Mughals, including the important fort of **Purandar**.
 
• In return, Shivaji was allowed to keep **12 forts** and was given the title of **Raja** by the Mughal emperor.
 
• Shivaji also agreed to serve the Mughal Empire as a **mansabdar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aga Khan**__

 __
 
• **Aga Khan** is a title used by the Imams of the **Nizari Ismaili Muslims**.
 
• The title was first given to **Hasan Ali Shah** by the Persian emperor Fath Ali Shah Qajar.
 
 
 
• **Shaista Khan**__
 __
 
• **Shaista Khan** was a Mughal general and the maternal uncle of Emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• He fought against Shivaji and was the **Subedar of Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **Malik Noor**__
 
 
• **Malik Noor** was not directly related to the Treaty of Purandar or to Shivaji's history.

questions.question: In which of the following locations did the 1920 Indian National Congress session take place?
questions.solution:

• The **1920 Indian National Congress session** was held in **Nagpur**.
 
• Indian National Congress was founded by **Allen Octavian Hume **with **Dada Bhai Naoroji** & **Dinshaw Wacha** in **1885**.
 
• On** 4 September 1920,** Congress met at Calcutta in a special session.
 
• **In December 1920,** Congress met once again in the Nagpur Session.
 
• This time the differences between CR Das had melted away.
 
• **He moved the main resolution of Non-cooperation.**
 
 
• A program of the surrender of titles, the boycott of schools, courts, and councils, the boycott of foreign goods, the promotion of maintenance of Hindu-Muslim unity, and strict non-violence was adopted.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The first session of INC took place in Bombay.
 
• The Viceroy of India during the formation of INC was Lord Dufferin.
 
• The only session of INC presided over by Mahatma Gandhi was "The Belgaum session" in 1924.
 
 
• It was the 39th session of INC.
 
 
 
• In this session, the basic necessities and concerns of the people of Karnataka were discussed and resolved.

questions.question: Where did Lord Mahavira attain salvation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pavapuri**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The salvation place of Mahavir Ji, the originator of the Jain religion is Pavapuri.**
 
• Pavapuri is located in the Nalanda district of Bihar.
 
• Pavapuri is a sacred place in Jainism as it was a cremation area of Mahavir Ji.
 
• The Jal Mandir meaning Water Temple, also known as Apapuri, in Pawapuri, meaning a town without sins, in the Indian state of Bihar.
 
 
• It is a highly revered temple dedicated to Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Jainism came into prominence in the 6th century B.C., when Lord Mahavira propagated the religion.
 
• There were 24 great teachers, the last of whom was Lord Mahavira.
 
 
• These twenty-four teachers were called Tirthankaras-people who had attained all knowledge (Moksha) while living and preached it to the people.
 
• The first Tirthankara was Rishabnatha.
 
 
 
• The word ‘Jain’ is derived from Jina or Jaina which means the ‘Conqueror’.

 Monuments
 Builders

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jama Masjid at Delhi:** Built by **Shah Jahan**, this mosque is one of the largest in India. It was constructed between 1650–1656 and is a prominent example of Mughal architecture.
 
• **Allahabad Fort:** Built by **Akbar** in 1583, this fort is located at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. Known for its massive structure, it showcases the grandeur of the Mughal architectural style.
 
• **Quila I Kunhan Masjid:** This mosque was constructed by **Sher Shah Suri** during his reign. It is situated within the Purana Qila in Delhi and represents the Indo-Islamic architectural style.
 
• **Jama Masjid at Sambhal:** Built by **Babur**, this mosque is an example of early Mughal architecture in India and reflects the simplicity yet elegance of the era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shah Jahan**__

 __
 
• Shah Jahan was known for his patronage of architecture and built some of the most iconic monuments, including the **Taj Mahal** and the **Red Fort.**
 
• His reign marked the pinnacle of Mughal architectural achievement.
 
 
 
• **Akbar**__
 __
 
• Known for his administrative reforms and religious tolerance, **Akbar** also contributed significantly to Mughal architecture.
 
• Some of his notable constructions include the **Fatehpur Sikri** complex and the **Buland Darwaza.**
 
 
 
• **Sher Shah Suri**__
 __
 
• Sher Shah Suri is remembered for his administrative efficiency and architectural contributions, including the construction of **roads** like the Grand Trunk Road.
 
• He also built several mosques and forts during his reign.
 
 
 
• **Babur**__
 
 
• **Babur**, the founder of the Mughal Empire, introduced Mughal architecture in India.
 
• His structures were relatively simple yet set the foundation for the elaborate designs of later rulers.

questions.question: With reference to Pala Dynasty which of the following is **not **correct?

options.text: Khalimpur inscription is an important source for the Pala Dynasty.
The Pala rulers adopted the title like Parameshwar, Paramvattaraka, and Maharajadhiraja.
Govindapala was the founder of Pala dynasty.
Vikramashila University was built by Dharmapala.

questions.solution:
The wrong option with reference to the Pala Dynasty is option 3) Govindapala was the founder of Pala dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 **Pala** dynasty, ruled in** Bihar** and **Bengal** from the **8th to the 12th century**. 
 
 
• 
 During a period of anarchy in the mid 8th century, **Gopala**, a local chieftain rose to power and laid the foundation of the Pala dynasty. 
 
 
• 
 Gopala was succeeded by **Dharmapala**.
 
 
• 
 Dharmapala assumed the greatest imperial titles of the period, including** Paramabhattaraka, Paramesvara and Maharajadhiraja.**
 
 
• 
 Dharmapala was succeeded by **Devapala, **who further expanded the empire to the Eastern India,including the kingdoms of **Assam, Odisha, and Kamarupa.**
 
 
• 
 After Devapala, the Pala power considerably decilned in the late 9th century.
 
 
• 
 It was again restored by** Mahipala I** whose reign could be dated back to late 10th century. 
 
 
• 
 The last known important king of the Pala dynasty was **Ramapla. **
 
 
• 
 The Palas were staunch supporters of **Mahayana Buddhism** and various Mahaviharas, stupas, chaityas, temples, and forts were built by them. 
 
 
• 
 Art and architecture flourished under the Palas in Bengal and Bihar. 
 
 
• 
 
**Sompaura Mahavira** and **Vikramshila Vihara** , both built by Dharmapala are some of the notable examples of Pala architectural excellence. 

 

**Thus, Govindapala__ was not the founder of the Pala dynasty.**

questions.question: In which year was Mahatma Gandhi imprisoned for the first time in Sabarmati Central Jail?
questions.solution:

• In **1922**__,__** Mahatma Gandhi**__ was __**imprisoned**__ for the first time in __**Sabarmati Central Jail**__.

 __
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** was arrested on **10 March 1922** at **Sabarmati Ashram Ahmedabad **for writing **three articles** for his newspaper **Young India**.
 
• He was sentenced to **six years imprisonment**.
 
• However, he eventually went on to serve **two years** of that term.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He was an** Indian lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer**.
 
• He became the l**eader of the nationalist movement **against the British rule of India.
 
• He was known as the **Father of the Nation**.
 
• **Gandhi **is internationally esteemed for his doctrine of **Satyagraha **and **Non- Violence** to achieve **political **and **social goals**.
 
• His **autobiography **is titled **My Experiments with Truth**.

• **Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)**
 
• **Kheda Movement (1918)**
 
• **Khilafat Movement (1919)**
